\[
P_i = \frac{\lambda - \alpha_i}{\beta_i}.

The two given operating points determine the four unknown coefficients. For unit 1,

\[
10000 - \alpha_1 = 50\beta_1, \qquad 10600 - \alpha_1 = 80\beta_1.
\]

Subtracting these equations yields \(\beta_1 = 20\), after which \(\alpha_1 = 9000\). Thus

\[
\text{IC}_1 = 9000 + 20P_1.
\]

For unit 2 the same procedure gives \(\beta_2 = 50\) and \(\alpha_2 = 6000\), so

\[
\text{IC}_2 = 6000 + 50P_2.
\]

\[

\]

\[
P_2 = \frac{11800 - 6000}{50} = 116\ \text{MW}.

\[
P_\text{total} = 100 + 116 = 216\ \text{MW}.
